security_spec.violation_condition: FreeBSD kernel code uses CSRRC/CSRRS (or immediate variants) on a pmpaddr CSR to atomically modify a subset of writable bits, causing bits that read-as a different value than their underlying value (e.g., pmpaddr[G-1] reading as 0 while underlying value is 1) to be silently written back with the read-value, corrupting the PMP region's address bound.
security_spec.summary: Read-modify-write CSR instructions (CSRRS/C) on pmpaddr corrupt underlying bits that read-as a different value, silently shrinking or relocating PMP regions and potentially weakening inter-domain memory isolation enforced by FreeBSD's pmap or bhyve

findings.finding: FreeBSD defines csr_set/csr_clear macros that expand to CSRRS/CSRRC (or CSRRSI/CSRRCI) instructions, but no call site in the entire sys/ tree invokes these macros on a pmpaddr CSR. PMP management is fully delegated to OpenSBI in M-mode; the kernel never reads or writes pmpaddr CSRs at all.

CSR_PMPADDR0-15 and CSR_PMPCFG0-3 constants are defined with DECLARE_CSR() for completeness, but no kernel code references them in csr_set/csr_clear calls. They exist solely as CSR number definitions.
CSRC/CSRCI/CSRS used on sstatus (for SSTATUS_SUM, SSTATUS_SIE), not on any PMP CSR. No pmpaddr corruption risk.
findings.snippet:
csrc sstatus, t0    # SSTATUS_SUM
csrci sstatus, (SSTATUS_SIE)
csrs sstatus, a4    # SSTATUS_SIE

findings.finding: CSRS/CSRC used on sstatus (for SSTATUS_FS) to enable/disable FPU access during context switch. No PMP CSR manipulation.
findings.snippet:
csrs sstatus, t0    # SSTATUS_FS_INITIAL
csrc sstatus, t0    # SSTATUS_FS_MASK
